items.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.raw_text: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026". They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5. Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others. Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58). This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier. I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August: llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace). Yes, please. Rocketing to Mars in a fraction of the time? Sounds great, but how close are we, really? In the new Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review , we ran progress reports on six potentially transformative technologies and ideas that have been “just around the corner” for years, or even decades. From exercise in a pill to nuclear-powered spaceships, we asked experts what’s holding them back and how far they’ve come. Check out our stories on how they all stacked up . Over the coming days, we’ll unpack each of the six technologies in The Download. So stay tuned! items.title: Valuing Public Libraries in New Brunswick: New Possibilities Using Linked Administrative Data
items.raw_text: Researchers in New Brunswick linked public library user records with health card–based provincial administrative data to study how library use relates to educational, health, and community outcomes. The study found that people who use the library tend to have better educational and developmental outcomes, with library-using families and recent immigrants being particularly engaged users. The researchers also found associations between library use and positive community outcomes, though they caution that this does not prove library use caused those outcomes. See the full report

items.title: Libraries my love, an Impact Report of Milan Public Libraries
items.raw_text: The City of Milan has published the first Impact Report of Milan Public Libraries . The study highlights the role of libraries as essential public spaces that foster social inclusion, participation, learning and community well-being. The document analyzes the profound civic, social, and cultural value that the Milan library network bring to the city’s diverse neighborhoods. The project employs a hybrid methodology combining quantitative data with qualitative research, including user surveys and focus groups. The findings highlight libraries as essential hubs for community integration, digital inclusion and lifelong learning, operating as free, accessible sanctuaries against urban isolation. This reports aligns with the spirit of the European Union’s major report, “Strengthening Europe through Public Libraries,” published in 2026 by the Open Method of Coordination (OMC) expert group. While the OMC report calls for European public libraries to be formally recognized as critical social infrastructure—vital for democratic cohesion, community resilience, and digital inclusion—Milan’s study provides empirical proof. “Biblioteca Amore Mio” directly demonstrates how the strategic axes and policy recommendations set by the European Commission are successfully translated into real-world, neighborhood-level social impact. NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
items.raw_text: During a lengthy news conference on Friday, NASA provided a detailed overview of how it plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface as soon as 2028 as part of its Artemis Program. Although much of the information behind these plans has been previously reported at Ars Technica and elsewhere, this marked the first time NASA has laid them out in detail and acknowledged some substantial changes in the architecture. Most notably, for SpaceX's Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. And for Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings. Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allows for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit. Read full article Comments

items.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
items.raw_text: Using Google's products and services has always been fundamentally precarious—doing so gives the world's largest advertising company a lot of juicy personal data. Google has long said it won't use the sensitive data from products like Gmail, Drive, and Photos for ad personalization, but a change to the company's privacy policy appears to dismantle that firewall. On October 16, Google issued an update to its privacy policy , spotted by Android Authority . The ad personalization section used to include a clear limit on data from certain apps. "We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos," the document said. Now, Google has updated it with the following language. Updated language on when your sensitive data might inform ads. Credit: Google This equivocation opens the door to using data from apps like Gmail and Photos in ads when it's shared with other Google services, and it just so happens Google has a mechanism for doing that, with Personal Intelligence. The company released Personal Intelligence in early 2026 , allowing users to hand data from multiple apps to Google AI products. The idea is that the added context from your existing data will lead to better AI answers, but it's also proving to be a privacy minefield. Read full article Comments

items.title: Inside the Pentagon, the pressure is on to find a home for a new spaceport
items.raw_text: Leaders in the US Space Force would like to have a new spaceport up and running in four years, adding a third heavy-lift launch site to relieve pressure from bases in Florida and California that have shot rockets into orbit for nearly 70 years. The obvious problem with that ambition is 2030 is four years away, and Pentagon officials have not determined where the new spaceport should go or how to acquire land for it. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink first mentioned the service's search for a third launch base in May. A congressionally mandated study of the Space Force's launch infrastructure identified the need for "another site that's capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability," Meink said in a House Armed Services Committee hearing. Those who fail to scan the address verification QR code within seven days will see their account demoted to the free tier and be barred from joining any other Duo or Family plan for 12 months. Spotify's QR code plan enforcement. Credit: Spotify Spotify's support documentation verifies the policy after users on Reddit began posting reports of receiving the QR prompt. The enforcement stems from Spotify's requirement that family plan members reside at the same address—a seemingly reasonable policy in concept. But what if you have a child away in college, a spouse who works on the road, or any number of other circumstances that might see families separated by physical distance? The policy could extend beyond friend groups looking to save a buck, affecting actual families who thought they were using the program as intended. items.title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
items.raw_text: Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision. But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions. “This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?” Read full article Comments

Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
items.raw_text: US chip champion Intel was so confused by the US government ban on foreign-made robots that it requested and received a waiver “out of an abundance of caution.” The tech company wanted to make sure that it could continue using certain robotic vehicles in its US chip fabs. The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request. On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year. The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors. Read full article Comments

items.title: RFK Jr.’s vaccine injury clinic could damage NIH hospital, board warns
items.raw_text: At a recent meeting of the board that oversees the National Institutes of Health's Clinical Center Research Hospital, chair Jack Leslie opened with cheerful introductions and gregarious chatter—then diverted from the agenda of the regularly scheduled meeting. He spent the next six minutes delivering a pointed rebuke of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, warning that his anti-vaccine activities could tarnish the venerable hospital, often called the "house of hope" for patients with rare conditions or those who have exhausted all other options. Leslie took issue with a recent stunt Kennedy had pulled at the hospital, which involved making a surprise appearance for a ribbon-cutting ceremony to open his signature vaccine injury clinic . The ceremony included a panel with people claiming to have been injured by vaccines. They sat behind placards reading "vaccine injured" and spoke with Kennedy and other high-ranking Trump administration officials. Leslie prefaced his comments by noting that some might prefer he not speak out against Kennedy's efforts. "But I think that that would be a failing as an advisory board if we were silent," he said. Leslie also noted that he has no concerns about studying potential injuries from vaccines. "Serious reactions are rare, but real," he said, and people who believe they've been injured should "be taken seriously." Read full article Comments

items.title: Knicks sent employees fake offer of championship rings in phishing test: Report
items.raw_text: The New York Knicks organization sent employees a phishing email promising free championship rings in a test of its staff's ability to detect scams, The New York Times reported yesterday. “Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here,” the email sent in late September said, instructing employees to click a link to make a selection from two ring designs. Madison Square Garden employees who clicked that link "were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class to help satisfy some of [owner James] Dolan’s growing cybersecurity concerns," the report said, citing team sources. Dolan is the owner of the Knicks, the New York Rangers, and Madison Square Garden. It's common for corporations to send phishing emails to find out which employees don't pay attention to clues that an email is a scam. A cybersecurity-test email often appears to be from the company itself but includes telltale signs of phishing. For example, Ars Technica owner Condé Nast sends phishing-test messages from email addresses with a misspelled domain, "condenest.com." Read full article Comments

items.title: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
items.raw_text: Gamers still hoping against hope for a true follow-up to Half-Life 2 (after so, so many years ) may remember last year's flurry of speculation that Half-Life 3 was finally nearing completion . Amid all those rumors, though, we never got any official sign from anyone inside Valve that a Half-Life project was currently in development. That changed this week thanks to an apparent slip-up during a panel at GameSoundCon , an industry conference devoted to "the art, technology, and business of game audio." In a panel devoted to Valve's use of open audio engines (captured in this Vimeo clip ), Valve composer and audio artist Mike Morasky let an interesting string of three letters slip while talking about the way the company implements high dynamic range (HDR) audio: Our HDR system is basically that's one of the three pieces that come together to make an HDR that you can easily optimize. And in fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version , so on and so forth [emphasis added]. "HLX," of course, has been widely reported as the internal code name for Valve's next Half-Life project. The codename has shown up in Valve engine code since at least 2024 , but it has never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until now (though Morasky was responsible for a close call in an interview last year). items.raw_text: US regulators have issued a warning to a nuclear project critical to Donald Trump’s efforts to revive the industry, after a contractor fell into a reactor cavity and a bundle of fuel rods nearly tipped over during refueling. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission told Holtec International, a company racing to reopen a shuttered reactor at the Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan, to address a “chilled work environment” that has made staff hesitant to raise safety concerns without fear of retaliation. The warning has prompted concerns among critics that financial and political pressures to revitalize nuclear power as an answer to booming AI-driven energy demand are increasing risks of accidents. items.title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics with satellites
items.raw_text: Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service has played a pivotal role in supporting Ukraine’s successful resistance to Russia’s full-scale invasion for years. But with Starlink having become increasingly unreliable due to Musk’s political inclinations and the latest surprise disruptions to service in Ukraine, the Ukrainians and Europe as a whole are now facing urgent questions about how to move forward without it. As the world’s largest communications satellite network, Starlink can typically support high-speed Internet and data streams for any user or vehicle equipped with a relatively compact Starlink terminal. This has enabled Ukraine to maintain vital communications for both civilian purposes and military operations—and has also expanded the Ukrainian military’s capability to remotely control or provide guidance to drones used in both air defense against Russian attacks and for striking back at Russian targets. “Starlink currently offers some of the best satellite coverage available, with virtually no competitors when you consider the combination of cost, availability, and ease of use,” according to the head of hardware R&D at the Ukrainian defense company BlueBird Tech , who provided comments to Ars anonymously for security reasons. “In practical terms, the main limitation is the need to position the antenna so it can receive signals from the satellites.” Read full article Comments

items.title: Review: Crystal Lake suffers a bit from its obsession with Pam Voorhees
items.raw_text: Peacock series Crystal Lake doesn’t feel like a Friday the 13th movie when you first press play, even though it’s set up to be a prequel to the original film. (This review includes spoilers of the original Friday the 13th movie but avoids major Crystal Lake spoilers.) Instead, Crystal Lake strives to build a drama that’s half homage, half uncharted territory, while giving a long-awaited backstory to Pamela Voorhees. The original villain in the first film, Pam Voorhees, shocked audiences in 1980 by popping up out of nowhere in the midst of a brutal camp counselor killing spree, then confronting the final girl with a Norman Bates-like delivery of the movie’s chilling tagline, “Kill her, mommy,” using the voice of her drowned son, Jason. Betsy Palmer as Pam Voorhees in Friday the 13th . Credit: via Paramount Pictures Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees in Crystal Lake. Credit: via Peacock Although the hockey-masked killer, Jason Voorhees, became the horror icon at the center of the franchise, his mom, Pam, continued to fascinate fans, who knew very little about her. Beheaded in the first film after just 13 minutes onscreen, her spirit would occasionally appear in later films, but the original actor, Betsy Palmer, who portrayed Pam refused to return, largely because the character has no depth. Finse autoriteiten hebben ingegrepen en het bedrijf opgedragen bepaalde werkzaamheden stil te leggen. De zaak draait om locaties in Muhos en Otanmäki in Noord-Finland, waar Google nieuwe datacenters wil ontwikkelen als onderdeel van zijn wereldwijde uitbreiding van cloud- en ai-capaciteit. Voor de voorbereidingen werden grote stukken bos gerooid. Volgens Finse media gaat het om honderden hectares natuurgebied en honderdduizenden bomen, schrijft The Guardian in een reportage/filmverslag . De Finse toezichthouder oordeelde dat de werkzaamheden te ver waren gevorderd terwijl de milieueffectrapportage nog niet volledig was afgerond. Daarop volgde een bevel om onderdelen van het project voorlopig stop te zetten. Natuurorganisaties en omwonenden uiten zorgen over de gevolgen voor biodiversiteit, waterhuishouding en het lokale landschap. Met 145 nieuwe datacenters in verschillende stadia van planning bevindt Finland zich in de voorhoede van de nieuwste expansiegolf van technologiebedrijven. Naast de relatief gunstige geopolitieke en geologische stabiliteit en de ruime beschikbaarheid van grond, maakt ook het koele klimaat het land bijzonder aantrekkelijk, omdat dat helpt de energiekosten laag te houden, schrijft de Britse krant. items.title: Microsoft slaat alarm over ai-cyberaanvallen
items.raw_text: Agentic-ai-platforms maken cyberaanvallen sneller dan ooit: organisaties hebben soms maar drie uur om aanvallers tegen te houden die het op hun cloudomgeving hebben voorzien. Microsoft slaagt hierover alarm tegenover ciso’s. Microsoft hield afgelopen woensdag spoedoverleg met zo’n tweehonderd ciso’s uit de hele wereld waaronder Dimitri van Zantvliet, ciso en directeur Cybersecurity bij NS en voorzitter van het CISO-platform Nederland . Volgens Microsoft moeten bedrijven en instellingen zich versneld voorbereiden op een nieuwe golf van cyberaanvallen. Aanleiding is de opkomst van platforms waarbij een heel leger van ai-agenten met ieder verschillende taken in een razend tempo doelwitten aanvallen. Die agenten gebruiken daarbij een veelheid aan hacking-tools. Met zo’n platform kunnen cybercriminelen en staatshackers krachtige ‘large language models’ (llm) aansturen om continu naar kwetsbaarheden in netwerken te zoeken. Vooral het Chinese platform Artex maakt zo handig gebruik van de collectieve kracht uit grote taalmodellen zoals die van OpenAI, Anthropic en het Chinese DeepSeek. Artex De Chinese cybersecurity-expert Li Puhua ontwikkelde Artex oorspronkelijk om kwetsbaarheden in netwerken op te sporen. Afgelopen juli maakte hij de tool gratis online beschikbaar. Daarna pasten hackers deze tool aan en zetten deze in voor kwaadaardige doeleinden.
